fix: escape user text in pydantic_evals report tables

Case names, inputs, outputs, expected output, metadata, score/label/metric
names, reasons, evaluator failures, case failure messages and the output of
a custom `RenderValueConfig` formatter went into Rich table cells as markup.
A stray closing tag such as `[/INST]` raised `MarkupError`, and text that
looks like a tag (`list[int]`, `[red]`, pydantic's `[type=..., input_value=...]`
error details) was dropped.

Escape that text with `rich.markup.escape`, keeping the renderer's own
`[bold]`, `[magenta]`, `[red]` and `[i]` markup. `escape` also doubles a
single trailing backslash so that a closing tag right after the text still
works; drop that extra backslash, which would otherwise show in every cell
ending in one, and double trailing backslashes only where the renderer puts
a closing tag right after user text.

The failures-table block in `EvaluationReport.print()` and the
`diff_formatter` branch of `_ValueRenderer.render_diff()` are now covered by
tests, so drop their `# pragma: no cover`.

`EvaluationReport.print()` treats report text as Rich markup: `[/INST]` raises `MarkupError`

### Initial Checks

- [x] I'm using the [latest version](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases/latest) of Pydantic AI
- [x] I've searched for my issue in [the issue tracker](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/issues) before opening this issue

### Description

`EvaluationReport.render()` and `print()` pass case names, inputs, outputs, labels and error messages to Rich as markup, so brackets are read as style tags.

- An unmatched closing tag like `[/INST]` (from a leaked Llama/Mistral chat template) in a case name, label value, or task or evaluator error raises `MarkupError` with default arguments, after the whole eval has run.
- Other tag-like text is dropped silently: a case named `parse list[int]` shows as `parse list`.

I'd expect the text to be printed as written.

#3975 tried to fix error messages in January but went stale before getting a test. My fix escapes this text with `rich.markup.escape`, keeps the report's own styling and has regression tests; I'll open a PR. I left report analyses, the title and the progress bar (separate code, same issue) out to keep it small.

### Minimal, Reproducible Example

```python
from pydantic_evals import Case, Dataset


def task(inputs: str) -> str:
    if inputs == 'crash':
        raise ValueError('model emitted "[/INST]" instead of JSON')
    return 'use list[str] here'


dataset = Dataset(name='markup', cases=[Case(name='parse list[int]', inputs='ok')])
dataset.evaluate_sync(task, progress=False).print(include_output=True)
# Case ID shows "parse list", Outputs shows "use list here"

dataset = Dataset(name='markup', cases=[Case(name='c1', inputs='crash')])
dataset.evaluate_sync(task, progress=False).print()
# raises rich.errors.MarkupError
```

### Logfire Trace

_No response_

### Python, Pydantic AI & LLM client version

- Python: 3.12.14
- Pydantic AI: pydantic-evals 2.52.0 (also on `main` at 1ef8834)
- LLM provider SDK: none; rich 15.0.0

Stop `EvaluationReport.render()` and `print()` from parsing case, task and evaluator text as Rich markup - Closes #9543 ### Why we make these changes `EvaluationReport.render()` and `print()` passed every user-supplied string in the case and failure tables to Rich as markup (#9543). A closing tag like `[/INST]` raised `MarkupError` after the eval had already run, and text that looks like a tag (`list[int]`, pydantic's `[type=..., input_value=...]` error details) disappeared. This escapes that text with `rich.markup.escape` and keeps the renderer's own `[bold]`, `[magenta]`, `[red]` and `[i]` markup. Because `escape` also doubles a single trailing backslash (so that a closing tag right after it still works), `_escape_markup` drops that extra backslash and `_style_markup` doubles trailing backslashes only where the renderer adds a closing tag itself. #3975 used `Text()` for the failures table, but that doesn't fit cells that mix user text with the renderer's markup, like diff cells and the red evaluator names. ### New public surface none ### User-visible behavior With the example from the issue: ```diff # case 'parse list[int]', task returns 'use list[str] here', report.print(include_output=True) -│ parse list │ use list here │ 324µs │ +│ parse list[int] │ use list[str] here │ 273µs │ # task raises ValueError('model emitted "[/INST]" instead of JSON'), report.print() -rich.errors.MarkupError: closing tag '[/INST]' at position 27 doesn't match any open tag +│ c1 │ ValueError: model emitted "[/INST]" instead of JSON │ ``` ### Verification - `tests/evals/test_reporting.py::test_render_shows_bracketed_text_verbatim` covers every user-supplied column of the case table and a case failure's name, inputs, error message and stacktrace. It now runs the failures-table block in `EvaluationReport.print()`, so I removed that block's `# pragma: no cover`. - `test_render_diff_shows_bracketed_text_verbatim` covers the baseline diff, including a bracketed label name inside the `[bold]` wrapper. - `test_render_diff_shows_custom_formatter_text_verbatim` covers a custom `value_formatter` and `diff_formatter`. It runs the `diff_formatter` branch of `_ValueRenderer.render_diff()`, so that `# pragma: no cover` is gone too. - `test_render_shows_trailing_backslashes_as_written` covers text ending in backslashes, both at the end of a cell and before the diff style's closing tag. - The first three raised `MarkupError` before this change; the last one showed `x → C:\temp[/]`. ### What changes for existing users Bracketed text in the case and failure tables is shown as written instead of raising or disappearing; that includes text returned by a `RenderValueConfig` `value_formatter` or `diff_formatter`, so markup returned from one on purpose now shows as tags, and `print(console=Console(markup=False))` now shows the escaping backslash (`list\[int]`). ### Checklist - [x] No **breaking changes** in accordance with the [version policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/version-policy.md). - [ ] Any permitted **compatibility impact** has a label, warning, migration, release note, and exact API-check waiver. (Left for you: returning markup from a `RenderValueConfig` formatter isn't documented, so I don't think it needs the label, but that's your call.) - [x] **PR title** is fit for the [release changelog](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
